words.example: Interest in the neighborhood began to burgeon after the new transit line opened.

words.meaning: to make a problem or its effects less severe without removing the underlying cause
words.example: The temporary discount may palliate customer frustration, but it will not fix the billing errors.

words.meaning: to transform something into a different form or nature
words.example: She managed to transmute a tense disagreement into a productive planning session.

words.meaning: to redirect a strong or unacceptable impulse into a constructive activity
words.example: He learned to sublimate his competitive streak into careful preparation for client pitches.

words.meaning: to respond to an accusation by making an accusation in return
words.example: Instead of trying to recriminate, both managers focused on how to prevent another missed deadline.

phrases.meaning: an informal way to reject an idea, excuse, or attitude completely
phrases.example: Miss me with that 'we have always done it this way' excuse; the process clearly needs work.

phrases.meaning: feels more powerful, meaningful, or enjoyable in a particular situation
phrases.example: That first cup of coffee after a red-eye flight just hits different.

phrases.meaning: save evidence of what was said or done so it can be proved later
phrases.example: If the vendor keeps changing its promises, keep the receipts and document every email.

phrases.meaning: state an opinion boldly and confidently instead of holding back
phrases.example: If you really think the proposal will fail, say it with your chest and explain why.

phrases.meaning: follow through firmly on your words, responsibilities, or principles
phrases.example: She said she would protect the team's focus time, and she stood on business when new requests arrived.
